content.title: How to make Nigerian okra soup
content.summary: Cook a rich okra soup with assorted meat, fish, prawns and a pepper-and-crayfish base.
requirements: Assorted meat and a rich meat stock
Stockfish, smoked fish and fresh prawns
Scotch bonnet, red bell pepper, onion and garlic
steps: Blend about one third of the okra and chop the rest. Clean the fish and prawns, then keep them aside.
Cook the tougher meats and stockfish first. Add the softer meats later so everything becomes tender without falling apart. Save the cooking stock.
Remove the cooked meat. Bring the stock and palm oil to a boil for about 6 to 8 minutes.
Add the blended peppers, iru, crayfish and chopped peppers. Cook for about 3 minutes.
Stir in the blended okra, then return the meat and fish to the pot.
Add the chopped okra and fresh prawns. Cook for about 5 minutes, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
tips: Blending some of the okra helps the soup draw while the chopped okra keeps its texture.
warnings: Add delicate fish near the end and stir gently so it does not break apart.
Check that the meat and prawns are fully cooked before serving.
sources: Sisi Jemimah — Nigerian Okra Soup: https://sisijemimah.com/2015/10/30/nigerian-okra-soup/ (checked 29 September 2026)
variations: Palm oil can be reduced or left out, and leafy vegetables can be added near the end.

content.title: How to make Nigerian jollof rice
content.summary: Cook long-grain rice in tomato stew and seasoned chicken stock for a classic Nigerian jollof rice.
requirements: Seasoning cubes, thyme and Nigerian curry powder
steps: Prepare the tomato stew. Season and cook the chicken, saving its stock, then grill or fry the chicken if you want a browned finish.
Parboil the rice, rinse it and drain it well.
Bring the chicken stock and tomato stew to a boil in a roomy pot.
Add the rice, curry powder, pepper and salt. Keep the liquid around the same level as the rice.
Cover and cook over low to medium heat until the rice absorbs the liquid.
Check the grains. If they are still firm, add a small amount of water, reduce the heat and cook until tender.
tips: Use a pot with enough room for the rice to cook evenly.
Add extra water a little at a time so the rice does not become soggy.
warnings: Keep the heat low enough to prevent the bottom from burning before the rice is cooked.
Make sure the chicken is cooked through.
sources: All Nigerian Recipes — Nigerian Jollof Rice: https://www.allnigerianrecipes.com/rice/nigerian-jollof-rice/ (checked 29 September 2026)
variations: The stock can come from chicken, turkey or another meat, but its seasoning will change the final taste.

content.title: How to make Nigerian beef stew
content.summary: Make a tomato-and-pepper stew with seasoned beef that can be served with rice and other staples.
requirements: Fresh tomatoes, red bell peppers and habanero peppers
Thyme, curry powder, bay leaf, seasoning and salt
steps: Season the beef with onion, garlic, ginger, thyme, curry powder, seasoning and salt. Cook until tender and save the stock.
Fry or grill the cooked beef until browned, then set it aside.
Blend the tomatoes, peppers, onion, garlic and ginger. Cook the mixture down until much of its water has evaporated.
Heat oil and fry sliced onion, garlic and bay leaf. Add tomato paste if using it.
Add the reduced tomato-and-pepper mixture and fry it, stirring from time to time, until the raw sour taste is gone and the oil begins to separate.
Add beef stock and the remaining seasonings. Simmer for about 8 minutes.
Return the beef to the pot and simmer for another 3 to 5 minutes before tasting and adjusting the seasoning.
tips: Reducing the blended tomatoes before frying shortens the frying time.
Keep the beef stock because it adds depth to the stew.
warnings: Hot oil and thick tomato sauce can splatter; use a deep pot and stir carefully.
Cook the beef fully and refrigerate leftovers promptly.
sources: Nigerian Food TV — Nigerian Beef Stew: https://www.nigerianfoodtv.com/nigerian-beef-stew-recipe-how-to-make-nigerian-stew-authentic-beef-stew-for-parties-and-jollof-rice/ (checked 29 September 2026)
variations: Pork can be used in place of beef, and rosemary, nutmeg or Cameroon pepper can be added to taste.

content.title: How to make Nigerian fried rice
content.summary: Cook seasoned rice, cool it, then stir-fry it with mixed vegetables and liver or another protein.
requirements: 3½ cups chicken, turkey or vegetable stock
Carrots, peas, sweetcorn and green beans
Curry powder, thyme, ginger, stock powder, pepper and salt
steps: Rinse the rice, then cook it in seasoned stock until it is only just tender. Spread or set it aside to cool.
Season and cook the liver or other protein, then cut it into small pieces.
Heat oil in a wide pan or wok over high heat. Stir-fry the onion and mixed vegetables so they remain bright and slightly crisp.
Add the protein and seasonings, then toss everything together.
Add the cooled rice in batches and stir-fry each batch until evenly coloured, hot and separate-grained.
tips: Use cooled rice and high heat to help the grains stay separate.
Cook in batches if your pan is small.
warnings: Do not overcook the rice before frying or it may turn mushy.
Cook liver and other meat fully before mixing them into the rice.
sources: Chef Lola's Kitchen — Nigerian Fried Rice: https://cheflolaskitchen.com/nigerian-fried-rice-recipe/ (checked 29 September 2026)
variations: Chicken, shrimp or extra vegetables can replace the liver.

content.title: How to make Nigerian egg rolls
content.summary: Wrap boiled eggs in a lightly spiced dough, chill them and fry them until golden.
requirements: ¼ cup lukewarm water and ⅓ cup milk
½ teaspoon yeast or baking powder
Salt, nutmeg, black pepper and cayenne pepper
steps: Mix the yeast and some of the sugar into the lukewarm water. Leave it for about 6 minutes until active.
Rub the butter into the flour, then mix in the remaining sugar, salt and spices.
Add the milk to the yeast mixture, then combine the wet and dry ingredients into a soft dough without overworking it.
Roll out the dough and cut it into portions large enough to wrap each boiled egg. Seal each egg completely.
Chill the wrapped eggs for about 1 hour so the dough firms up.
Fry in moderately hot oil, turning as needed, until evenly golden. Drain before serving.
tips: Seal the dough well so it does not open while frying.
Keep the oil at a steady medium heat so the dough cooks through before it gets too dark.
warnings: Lower the egg rolls into the oil carefully to avoid splashes.
Let the boiled eggs cool before wrapping them.
sources: Nigerian Lazy Chef — Nigerian Egg Rolls: https://nigerianlazychef.com/recipes/nigerian-egg-rolls/ (checked 29 September 2026)
variations: Baking powder can replace yeast, and the wrapped eggs can be baked instead of fried.
